verdict.rationale: Sentry documents a self-hosted, source-available setup that works out of the box, so developers can run their own instance. Community users confirm running it locally in Docker for debugging and installing it with a simple ./install.sh. However, the minimal setup comes with no guarantees or dedicated support, and hands-on reports describe it as heavy to run locally (16GB minimum) and increasingly complex. missing for 10: a lightweight, officially supported local/dev mode, and first-party docs on using a local instance specifically to test instrumentation and dashboards.

support.subject: As a developer, I can spin up a local or dev instance of the platform to test instrumentation and dashboards

citations.quote: How you can run all of Sentry on your own server, without paying anything.
